content.comment_body: Hello everyone, I'm encountering an issue with the maximum number of output connectors for User Defined Functions (UDF). Is there any workaround to increase this? I need 5 outputs from a UDF. Thank you.
No, currently the maximum is 8 inputs and 4 outputs for a UDF.

While not perfect, you could use an analog output as a workaround. For example, figure 1 shows the basic concept of using a multiplexer inside a UDF. In general, if you're needing more than 4 outputs, the UDF may become more complex than originally intended. This is just my opinion without knowing your exact use case.
It depends on the application—parameter I/O could work as well. I have a UDF for shifting analog values where I use 6 outputs.

Any solution that works is good; you could combine digital signals into a single byte using a multiplexer, pass this out of the UDF as an analog or parameter value, store it in memory, and then retrieve each one individually as needed in your network logic. [user_name] (translated with Google)
This solution has already been mentioned by other users. Check the previous posts above yours.
It's not exactly the same, but it's a similar approach.

analysis.insight_summary: A user encountered the limitation of only four output connectors for UDFs in [company_name]'s software. Community members confirmed this limitation, suggested alternatives such as analog multiplexing and parameter I/O adaptation, and discussed possible workarounds to address complex needs, emphasizing creative approaches when standard capabilities are insufficient.
analysis.user_expectations: The user hopes for more flexible options in UDF output connectors—expecting either higher limits or practical solutions to overcome this restriction for advanced or custom function requirements.
